title.text: desk-q Leases: from a section to signals

rule.text:
THE RULE FOR THE BUILDER

A lease reaches the Queue screen only when a person can act on it or must decide something.

• Healthy leases: nothing. The Leases section is removed from the Queue view (desk-q.mjs leaseLines and its call in overviewParts).
• A stuck (overdue) lease: one ▲ note in the existing notes list, tagged with the holder's repo, carrying the force-release command. Board 3.
• A would-refuse during the trial: one grey note naming who clashed with whom. Board 4.
• An unreadable lease store: one ▲ note, tag 'leases', with desk-env lease reset --reason <why>.
• Trial end: one /desk-needs-you item. Board 6.
• A running ticket's port: a Port row on its ticket screen. Board 5.

desk-env lease list stays the full table.

copy.text:
COPY RULES

• Say 'stopped checking in', not 'renew' or 'overdue'.
• Name the ticket (DS-796), never the pid or lease label.
• The command is the last thing on the note, on its own wrapped line, in bold.
• 'Trial' replaces 'shadow' wherever a person reads it.
• Times are local clock times (14:02), ages as desk-q already words them (1h 12m).

edge.text:
STATES TO TEST

• 0 leases, 1, 40: Queue screen looks identical (board 2).
• 2 stuck leases in one repo: two notes, each with its own command.
• A stuck slot lease (no ticket): name what it runs, e.g. 'A test run in DS-945's worktree'.
• Clashes on 3 kinds today: one note per kind, not per clash.
• A kind already on (not trial): its refusals are not notes; the refused worker waits and its row says so.
• Narrow terminal (80 cols): notes wrap under the text column like today.
